'''Ulrike Herzschuh''' is a German [[geoecology|geoecologist]] and [[palaeoclimatology|palaeoclimatologist]]. She leads the Polar Terrestrial Environmental Systems section at the [[Alfred Wegener Institute]] (AWI), Helmholtz Centre for Polar and Marine Research in Potsdam, a position she has held since 2012.<ref name="dfg-leibniz">{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Ulrike Herzschuh – Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prizewinner 2024 |url=https://www.dfg.de/en/funded-projects/prizewinners/leibniz-prize/2024/herzschuh |publisher=Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft |access-date=8 May 2026}}</ref><ref name="helmholtz">{{cite web |title=Leibniz Prize – Helmholtz Association |url=https://www.helmholtz.de/en/about-us/who-we-are/research-awards/leibniz-prize/ |publisher=Helmholtz Association of German Research Centres |access-date=8 May 2026}}</ref>

== Career ==
Herzschuh completed her doctorate at the [[Free University of Berlin]] in 2004. She then worked as a researcher at the [[University of Bergen]] in Norway before returning to Germany. In 2005 she was appointed junior professor of palaeoecology and palaeoclimatology at the [[University of Potsdam]].<ref name="uni-potsdam-profile">{{cite web |title=Extrapolating from the Core – Leibniz Prize winner Ulrike Herzschuh |url=https://www.uni-potsdam.de/en/headlines-and-featured-stories/detail/2024-10-07-extrapolating-from-the-core-leibniz-prize-winner-ulrike-herzschuh-conducts-research |publisher=University of Potsdam |date=7 October 2024 |access-date=8 May 2026}}</ref><ref name="geo-x">{{cite web |title=Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize: Congratulations to Prof. Dr. Ulrike Herzschuh (AWI) |url=https://www.geo-x.net/en/news/details/news/gottfried-wilhelm-leibniz-prize-congratulations-to-prof-dr-ulrike-herzschuh-awi/ |publisher=Geo.X |access-date=8 May 2026}}</ref>

She has been elected as Germany's representative on the international expert committees of the [[International Arctic Science Committee]] (IASC)<ref name="iasc">{{cite web |title=International Arctic Science Committee |url=https://iasc.info |publisher=IASC |access-date=8 May 2026}}</ref> and Conservation of Arctic Flora and Fauna (CAFF).<ref name="caff">{{cite web |title=Conservation of Arctic Flora and Fauna |url=https://www.caff.is |publisher=CAFF |access-date=8 May 2026}}</ref>

== Research ==
Herzschuh's work examines how climate fluctuations over geological time have affected biodiversity, particularly in Arctic and high-mountain environments. She conducts fieldwork in Siberia, Antarctica, the Tibetan Plateau, and Alaska, collecting sediment cores from lakes and marine deposits. These cores contain fossil pollen, chironomid midges, stable isotopes, and biomarkers that allow reconstruction of past climates.<ref name="awi-profile">{{cite web |title=Ulrike Herzschuh |url=https://www.awi.de/en/about-us/organisation/staff/single-view/ulrike-herzschuh.html |publisher=Alfred Wegener Institute |access-date=8 May 2026}}</ref><ref name="awi-epic">{{cite web |title=Publications by Ulrike Herzschuh |url=https://epic.awi.de/view/creators/Herzschuh=3AUlrike=3A=3A.html |publisher=Alfred Wegener Institute ePIC Repository |access-date=8 May 2026}}</ref>

Her group has contributed to developing methods for extracting ancient DNA (aDNA) from lake sediments to track changes in species composition over millennia. They have also developed individual-based vegetation models incorporating plant functional traits.<ref name="dfg-leibniz"/><ref name="researchgate">{{cite web |title=Ulrike Herzschuh – Research Profile |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Ulrike-Herzschuh |publisher=ResearchGate |access-date=8 May 2026}}</ref>

In 2018 she received an ERC Consolidator Grant for the project ''Glacial Legacy'' (grant no. 772852), which examined whether present-day plant distributions in Arctic and subarctic regions still reflect the influence of the last glacial period.<ref name="erc-grant">{{cite web |title=Glacial Legacy – ERC Consolidator Grant no. 772852 |url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/772852 |publisher=European Research Council |access-date=8 May 2026}}</ref>
